Most of our REST endpoints and GraphQL Admin API endpoints use the `X-Auth-Token` header to authenticate to BigCommerce servers. For more about the APIs that do NOT use the `X-Auth-Token` header, consult this article’s sections on dynamic tokens and same-origin CORS authentication .

The `X-Auth-Token` header uses access tokens to authenticate requests. Create an OAuth API account to generate access tokens. Pass the access token as the value of the `X-Auth-Token` header of the request you want to authenticate.

For a request to succeed, the access token’s API account must have permission to receive the response. Configure your API account with the minimum set of OAuth scopes that your implementation needs.

Merchants generate single-store API credentials when they create API accounts in their store control panel, in the Settings > Store-level API accounts†login.bigcommerce.com menu. Use these credentials to read and change one store’s data with BigCommerce’s APIs. You can’t change store-level access tokens or OAuth scopes.

  * An `access_token`, which accompanies most REST API requests.

You can create app-level API accounts in the Developer Portal†build.bigcommerce.com . After a store owner or authorized user installs and authorizes an app, most apps use access tokens generated from the API account’s client ID, client secret, and a temporary grant code to read and change store data. Generate access tokens with the BigCommerce-initiated grant code authorization flow.

text:
BigCommerce offers a suite of APIs that let you manage store data, sign customers in, make client-side queries for product information, and write apps that integrate third-party services into store operations.

BigCommerce offers three types of OAuth-based API accounts to developers who wish to use BigCommerce’s REST APIs: store-level credentials, app-level credentials, and account-level credentials. This section describes the difference between the three, how to obtain and revoke account credentials, and the use cases for each. It also contains a reference for available OAuth scopes and provides a compelling list of reasons to migrate from legacy API tokens to OAuth credentials.

text:
Authorization for the B2C Commerce API resources is handled not through user permissions, but through client permissions.

To authorize this wide range of client types, we’ve defined a set of scopes based on the OAuth 2.1 standard. The available scopes give you control over exactly what clients are authorized to do with the SCAPI Admin APIs and Shopper APIs.

text:
Find information about PitchBook’s API solution and discover how it can meet your business needs. Our API is a separate offering from the PitchBook Platform that requires a standalone contract agreement.

PitchBook’s API solution allows you to call specific PitchBook data into your internal business systems on demand. This flexible solution means you have access to PitchBook’s expansive database. It’s the ideal integration for CRM enrichment, allowing you to extract data on an ad-hoc basis that meets the needs of your organization.

The PitchBook API is a RESTful implementation that most HTTP clients can easily access in your chosen language or via a web browser. Every call will use the same base URL: https://api.pitchbook.com†api.pitchbook.com L38: Available data points

The API solution offers a variety of relational endpoints, including financing details, deal stock information, as well as AI-powered VC exit predictor data. See the full list from our API Endpoints Overview document.†pitchbook.highspot.com L40: 

To start your API connection, you will need to send a request directly to our Direct Data team through this link. L43: Or if you’re a PitchBook client, you can also head to the Plugins & Apps section from the My PitchBook section of the left-hand sidebar on the PitchBook Platform and choose PitchBook API.

Our team will work with you to understand the insights and data you’re looking for and help you establish the API connection through an API key or authentication token. Available data for each entity type is packaged across several endpoints so you can map the data to your desired format and structure.
